questions.stem: Class A has mean 65 and range 30. Class B has mean 72 and range 15. Which is the best comparison?

options.text: Class B performed better on average and was more consistent
Class A performed better on average but was less consistent
Class B performed better on average but was less consistent
Class A was more consistent and had a higher average

questions.explanation: Class B has a higher mean (72 > 65), so performed better on average. Class B has a smaller range (15 < 30), so scores were more consistent. When comparing distributions, always comment on both an average and a measure of spread.

questions.stem: Team X: median goals = 2, IQR = 3. Team Y: median goals = 3, IQR = 1. Which statement is correct?

options.text: Team X scores more goals on average
Team Y scores more goals on average and is more consistent
Team X is more consistent because they have a lower median
Team Y has more variation in their scores

questions.explanation: Team Y has higher median (3 > 2) so scores more on average. Team Y has lower IQR (1 < 3) so is more consistent. Lower IQR means the middle 50% of data is more tightly grouped.

questions.stem: Shop A's daily sales: mean = £450, range = £200. Shop B's daily sales: mean = £450, range = £80. Which shop's sales are more predictable?

options.text: Shop A, because it has the same mean
Shop B, because its range is smaller
Neither, because the means are equal
Shop A, because its range is larger

questions.explanation: Both shops have the same average sales (£450), but Shop B has a much smaller range (£80 vs £200), meaning daily sales vary less. Shop B's sales are therefore more predictable and consistent.

questions.stem: Which pair of statistics should you use to compare two data sets?

options.text: Mean and mode
An average (mean or median) and a measure of spread (range or IQR)
Range and IQR
Median and mean

questions.explanation: To compare distributions fully, use one measure of average (central tendency) AND one measure of spread (variation). This lets you compare both the typical value and the consistency. Using two averages or two spreads gives incomplete comparisons.

questions.stem: Data set P has median 40 and IQR 12. Data set Q has median 35 and IQR 20. Tom says 'Q is better because it has more variation.' Is Tom correct?

options.text: Yes, more variation is always better
No, P has a higher average and is more consistent
Yes, Q has a higher IQR which is better
No, but Q is better because it has a lower median

questions.explanation: More variation is not 'better' - it means less consistency. P has a higher median (40 > 35), meaning typical values are higher. P also has a smaller IQR (12 < 20), meaning it is more consistent. Whether higher values are 'better' depends on context.
